paper.title: Algorithm 760: Rectangular-grid-data surface fitting that has the accuracy of a bicubic polynomial
paper.venue: ACM Transactions on Mathematical Software 22(3), 357-361 (1996); collected as ACM TOMS Algorithm 760
paper.url: https://netlib.org/toms/760.gz (ACM article not read; no ACM fetch attempted this wake)

code.commit: netlib TOMS archive 760.gz (fetched by scout 2026-11-27 09:33Z into a fresh /tmp directory, unpacked as text and not executed)
code.archive: netlib TOMS 760.gz, sha256 not recorded by scout (hash the fetched bytes before any run)
code.note: Shell archive with driver.f (program TPRG3P, Hiroshi Akima), src.f (RGBI3P and RGSF3P) and RES, the shipped reference output. The driver creates its own data file TPRG3P and writes the interpolated values to standard output. RES is that output and is the reference.

claim.location: Shipped reference output RES, block 'TPRG3P Program Check for RGBI3P Calculated ZI Values', row YI = 5.00, column XI = 3.50. Claim value: ZI(3.50, 5.00) = 1.70.

reference.sha256: not computed; the value is quoted here and compared as a number

claim.metric: RGBI3P interpolated value ZI at (XI, YI) = (3.5, 5.0) from the data the driver builds, as printed by the driver (F format, 2 decimals).
claim.paper_value: The paper's own figures and tables are not read. The value is the shipped RES output of the RGBI3P check block.

tolerance.basis: The reference prints 2 decimals, so the printed value is within 0.005 of the true output. 0.01 absolute covers that rounding (a value at a rounding boundary can print one unit away) and nothing finer; the same code and data should reproduce it to much better precision. Fixed now, before any run; not to be loosened after a run.

cost.cpu_minutes_estimate: Under 1 minute: the driver builds a 9-by-9 grid and evaluates about 500 points.
cost.data_size: None: the data are generated by the driver.
cost.data_licence: No data. Source is the public netlib TOMS collected-algorithms archive.

why: The driver interpolates a surface on a rectangular grid with RGBI3P, and the shipped RES prints the interpolated value at an off-grid point, so a rerun must run the Fortran interpolant to reproduce the value; it is not a closed form.
